text:
sasha: Bringing OrpheusX-13B int4 into staging. Quick heads-up: saw a reproducible summarization regression on the news-summarize bench after row-wise int4 quant. Posting artifacts and short notes below.

jia: Can you drop the eval command and the numbers? :eyes:

sasha: Sure — command I ran (staging infra):
```
./run_eval --model orpheusx-13b --quant int4-rowwise --prompts news-summarize \n  --ckpt /mnt/models/orpheusx/step_4200 \n  --batch 8 --maxlen 512 --seed 42
```

eval-bot: automated run summary (2026-03-20T14:05Z):
- rouge1: baseline fp16=0.421 -> orpheusx:int4=0.370
- rougeL: 0.395 -> 0.346
- BLEU: 21.3 -> 18.1
- avg perplexity +5% on heldout set

matt: Oof, 4-5 point drop on rouge1 is significant. Did we apply the same rotary/freq params as in the model repo? :face_with_monocle:

sasha: We used runtime default (rotary_base=10000, freq_scale=1.0). Model config in the repo lists rotary_base: 4096 and a headwise freq_scale ~0.97. I failed to pick that up when converting.

omar: Also noticed tokenization weirdness during sampling. OrpheusX training data contained soft-hyphen (U+00AD) as a delimiter for linebreaks. Our normalizer strips U+00AD which shifts tokenization for hyphenated words -> embedding alignment mismatch. Small example: the string "co\u00ADop change" tokenizes in the original tokenizer as ["co\u00adh", "op", " change"] vs our tokenizer -> ["coop", " change"]. That can change attention patterns in early layers.

jia: Interesting — so two potential sources: rotary param mismatch + tokenizer normalizer removing soft-hyphen. Either could explain the quality regression. Which is cheaper to try first?

matt: Toggle rotary_base to 4096 in the runtime and rerun quick eval (small sample). That is low-risk. If that doesn't close the gap, try preserving U+00AD in normalization and run a micro-batch.

sasha: I ran a smoke with rotary_base=4096 and freq_scale=0.97 on a 200-example subset: rouge1 improved from 0.370 -> 0.401 (partial recovery). Still shy of 0.421 baseline.

omar: Good signal. Next step: re-run with tokenizer change (preserve soft-hyphen) on same subset to isolate impact. Also try combined (rotary + tokenizer).

sasha: I'll run tokenizer-preserve + combined runs tonight. Pushed an artifacts tar to s3: s3://redwood-staging/orpheusx/step_4200/artifacts/2026-03-20.tar.gz

jia: Please open an internal issue and tag eng-ml/infra. Put the three run IDs in the issue: quick-rotary, quick-preserve-soft, quick-combined.

sasha: Created issue #12347 and assigned to @omar. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/12347. Putting triage notes in the issue.

matt: Thanks. If tokenizer-preserve recovers most of the delta, we should add a conversion-time normalizer flag for soft-hyphen-preserve for models that used it.

omar: Agree. Also check kv-cache alignment after changing tokenization — small token shifts can cause cache eviction patterns in the serving runtime.

sasha: Noted. Will post final numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
